title: Interrupt Mask
body:
Three bits in the [[Motorola 68000]]'s [[Status Register]] holding the current
[[IPL|interrupt priority level]]. An incoming [[IRQs|IRQ]] is only taken if its level is
*higher* than the mask; anything at or below is held pending until the mask drops.

Set the mask to 7 and you have effectively disabled interrupts, which is how you protect a
critical section that an [[ISRs|ISR]] also touches. Level 7 itself is non-maskable, so it
gets through regardless.

Raising the mask on entry to an ISR is what stops a lower-priority device from interrupting
the handler for a higher-priority one.
